Three Permanent Cooling Centers, Sited Where Heat Hurts Most

The Municipal Decision Scenario (Atlanta, GA)

  • Who Is Asking: Dana, Mayor's Office of Sustainability & Resilience (3:40 PM Tuesday; City Council votes in 3 weeks on the FY26 capital budget).
  • The Mandate: Allocate $600,000 to fund 3 permanent cooling centers ($180k/yr each) across 353 Atlanta census tracts.
  • The Microclimate Inequality: Airport forecasts report one city temperature, but 23,386 street-level Heat Watch readings (mean 82.06°F) show blocks 2 miles apart differ by up to 13.5°F (-5.79°F to +7.70°F offset).
  • Why Raw Sensors Fail Council: Siting on peak heat alone puts centers in rail yards or clusters all 3 in one district; siting on politics leaves car-free seniors unserved.
  • Our Solution: A Google Cloud ADK + BigQuery ML spatial decision assistant that predicts street-level heat offsets (°F above city mean), explains physical drivers, enforces non-overlapping catchments, and audits equity.
Speaker Note: "We chose Atlanta on the 'This Budget Cycle' track. Our planner has $600k to site 3 permanent cooling centers before Council votes in 3 weeks. We built an AI assistant that predicts microclimate heat offsets, proves who benefits, and survives a contested City Council hearing."

The Answer: 3 Non-Overlapping Sites + Why Site #4 Was Displaced

3 Funded Picks ($540k / $600k Cap · 12,260 Reached in 0.5 mi)

  • Offset, Never Raw Temperature: Ranks 5,618 candidate grid points (~250 m) by Predicted Offset (+°F vs. 82.06°F city mean) × 7-yr GHCN Hot Days (≥95°F) × Walkable Vulnerability with greedy ≥2.0 km spacing.
  • Site #1 · Mechanicsville (Tract 58.00 / 76.03): +4.4°F vs. city mean · 44 days/yr ≥95°F · 4,890 residents in 0.5 mi (28.4%–56.4% no-car, 16.2% 65+). ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT drivers: Impervious surface (+2.3°F), Street density (+1.4°F), Land-use mix (+1.0°F), Park proximity (-0.3°F).
  • Site #2 · Old Fourth Ward / Ashview (Tract 42.00): +3.9°F vs. city mean · 42 days/yr ≥95°F · 4,120 residents (24.1%–46.7% no-car, 17.8% 65+). Drivers: Impervious surface (+1.9°F), Street density (+1.4°F).
  • Site #3 · West End / Summerhill (Tract 48.00): +3.6°F vs. city mean · 41 days/yr ≥95°F · 3,250 residents (22.5%–38.0% no-car, 14.6%–24.2% 65+). Unmeasured tract predicted via BQML.
  • Why Not Site #4 (Bankhead / Midtown Edge)? Runs +3.1°F (39 days ≥95°F) but has less than half the car-free rate (12.4% vs. 28.4% at Site #1) and reaches 2,480 vs. 4,890 residents.
Speaker Note: "Notice two critical things: first, we predict thermal offset above the city mean—never fake point forecasts—and decompose every site into °F physical drivers via ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT. Second, we explicitly answer why runner-up Site 4 in Bankhead was passed over."

Technical Execution & Rigor · Google ADK + BigQuery ML + Managed MCP Toolbox
Slide 4 of 6
Architecture & Why You Can Trust It: Leak-Free Spatial Holdout

End-to-End Google Cloud Stack & Validation Rigor

  • Google ADK + Gemini 2.5 Flash: Multi-agent orchestrator calling custom Python tools (explain_heat_offset, select_cooling_center_sites, run_equity_audit) + GroundingVerifier.
  • Managed MCP Server (heat-toolbox): Cloud Run MCP Toolbox for Databases exposing parameterized SQL tools over a4i_semantic (dim_tract, site_hot_days, vulnerable_population) with least-privilege IAM (toolbox-sa, heat-agent-sa).
  • Where vs. How Often Separation: Heat Watch (23,386 readings, 100% NULL timestamps) answers spatial WHERE; 7-year NOAA GHCN daily history (17,452 station-days across 7 stations) answers temporal HOW OFTEN via site_hot_days(offset_f).
  • Defeating 1 Hz Spatial Leakage: Aggregated 23,386 points into 2,020 geohash-7 (~150 m) cells and held out 6 whole geohash-5 (~4.9 km) blocks (484 eval / 1,378 train). Excluded temp_f, heat_index_f, humidity_pct, and all race columns.
  • Verified BQML Performance: a4i_ml.offset_model_v1 beats predict-zero baseline on held-out spatial blocks (MAE = 1.254°F vs. 1.355°F; RMSE = 1.542°F vs. 1.622°F) and passes 13/13 SQL validation checks.
Speaker Note: "A random split on 1 Hz road readings leaks adjacent points and yields a fake 0.98 R². We aggregated to 150m geohash-7 cells, held out entire 5km geohash-5 spatial blocks, stripped all drive-day temperatures and race columns, and beat the baseline honestly (1.254°F vs 1.355°F MAE)."

Slide 5 of 6
Equity Audit: 4 of 4 Measures Confirm Need-Based Prioritization

Post-Hoc Equity Audit vs. Atlanta Baseline (353 Tracts)

  • Strict Ethical Guardrail (DEC-005): Race and ethnicity are never used in a4i_core, BQML training features, or site ranking. We audit recommended outputs post-hoc against a4i_semantic.audit_city_baseline.
  • Households Without a Vehicle: 25.0% in 0.5-mi catchment (50.41% in core tracts) vs. 8.23% Atlanta average → 3.0x to 6.12x higher transit dependency.
  • Poverty Rate: 31.8% in catchment (44.05% in core tracts) vs. 13.95% Atlanta average → 2.3x to 3.16x higher poverty concentration.
  • Seniors Aged 65+: 16.2% in catchment (19.44% in core tracts) vs. 12.47% Atlanta average → 1.3x to 1.56x higher senior vulnerability.
  • Median Household Income: $38,133 in catchment ($17,853 in core tracts) vs. $75,714 Atlanta average (50% to 76% below citywide median).
  • Post-Hoc ACS Racial Check (Output Only): Selected tracts are 90.81% Black residents vs. 41.66% citywide (2.18x), proving physical heat + transit siting reaches historically redlined neighborhoods without demographic bias in the model.
Speaker Note: "Race was never a model input. Yet when we run our post-hoc equity audit across all 353 Atlanta census tracts, our 3 recommended sites reach communities with 3.0x to 6.1x higher car-free households, 2.3x to 3.2x higher poverty, and half the citywide median income."

Slide 6 of 6
Human-in-the-Loop Council Memo, Honest Limits & Live Links

Why Custom UI, Honest Boundaries & Submission Links

  • Why Custom Next.js UI on Cloud Run: Planners defending a $600k vote need interactive Voronoi tract maps, Site 1 vs. Site 4 trade-off cards, and a Human-in-the-Loop sign-off memo (not a raw developer chat). Pinned min-instances=1.
  • Honest Refusal Gate (DEC-007): a4i_ml.point_features enforces in_footprint (≤500 m from Heat Watch route). Queries in Marietta (12.3 km out) or Chicago are refused honestly.
  • Known Model Limitations: (1) Single-day Heat Watch snapshot; (2) Predicts current exposure offset, cannot simulate cooling ΔT from planting new trees; (3) Straight-line 0.5-mi / 1.5-km buffers, not turn-by-turn walk isochrones; (4) 100% US Gov/CC0 data (zero OSM/ODbL).
